answer: Each wheel of cheese is stamped as it leaves the press, and the dairy keeper reads the rind mark against the cellar book before any wheel may be sold. A mirror wheel pressed in another glen carries the wrong stamp: at the forge of the cellar the rind must match the keeper's own die, and a foreign wheel smells of another dairy. Faking a cheese means keeping cows for a season, pressing 150 wheels and paying 8,600, while the reef stamp on the rind is checked at every market, so a wheel whose pressing was never stamped is thrown to the pigs.
